scheme_name: Financial Assistance for Encouraging Worker's Children's Participation in Cultural Activities- Haryana Labour Welfare Board
description:
The Financial Assistance for Encouraging Worker's Children's Participation in Cultural Activities is a welfare scheme initiated by the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

This scheme was launched on 1st April 2018.

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote cultural activities among the children of registered workers in the state of Haryana.

The scheme aims to encourage children's participation in various cultural events and activities that enhance their skills and talents.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board has set a target to provide financial assistance to at least 5,000 children annually under this scheme.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is specifically aimed at children who are engaged in cultural activities such as music, dance, drama, and other performing arts.

Each child can receive financial assistance of up to INR 10,000 per year.

This amount is intended to cover expenses related to participation in cultural events, training, and other associated costs.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are clearly defined.

Children of registered workers under the Haryana Labour Welfare Board are eligible to apply for this financial assistance.

The age limit for applicants is set between 5 years and 18 years.

To qualify for the scheme, the family income of the applicant should not exceed INR 3 lakh per annum.

This income limit ensures that the benefits are directed towards economically weaker sections of society.

Applicants must provide proof of their parent's registration as a worker with the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

Additionally, a certificate of participation in cultural activities from a recognized institution is required.

The application process for this scheme is straightforward.

Interested applicants must obtain the application form from the official website of the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

The application form can also be collected from the nearest Labour Welfare Office.

Once the form is filled out, it must be submitted along with the required documents.

The required documents include proof of income, proof of the parent’s registration, and the participation certificate.

The completed application must be submitted to the Labour Welfare Office in the respective district.

Applications are accepted throughout the year.

However, it is advisable to apply well in advance of any cultural event to ensure timely processing.

The disbursement of financial assistance is typically processed within 30 days of application approval.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board is responsible for implementing this scheme.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment, Government of Haryana.

For further assistance, individuals can contact the Haryana Labour Welfare Board at their official office.

The contact number for inquiries is +91-172-270-2000.

The official website of the Haryana Labour Welfare Board provides additional information and updates regarding the scheme.

The scheme has been well-received since its inception.

It has successfully encouraged many children to engage in cultural activities.

The board has reported that over 3,000 children received financial assistance in the first year of the scheme alone.

This number has steadily increased in subsequent years.

The initiative has also fostered a sense of community among workers and their families.

Cultural participation has been linked to improved social skills and self-esteem among children.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board continues to monitor the impact of this scheme on the children's development.

Feedback from beneficiaries has been positive, highlighting the importance of financial support in pursuing cultural interests.

The scheme aligns with the broader goals of the Government of Haryana to promote education and holistic development.

It also emphasizes the significance of cultural heritage and arts in the state.

The financial assistance is not just limited to traditional arts but also includes modern forms of cultural expression.

This flexibility allows children to explore diverse interests and talents.

The board encourages parents to actively support their children's participation in cultural activities.

Workshops and training sessions are often organized to help children develop their skills further.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board collaborates with various cultural organizations to enhance the reach of this scheme.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life for workers and their families.

Regular updates and reports on the scheme's progress are published on the Haryana Labour Welfare Board's website.

This transparency helps maintain accountability and encourages more families to take advantage of the benefits.

In conclusion, the Financial Assistance for Encouraging Worker's Children's Participation in Cultural Activities is a significant initiative by the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

It provides essential support to children from economically weaker backgrounds to pursue their cultural interests.

The scheme not only aids in financial terms but also promotes the overall development of children in Haryana.

By fostering cultural participation, the scheme contributes to the preservation of the rich cultural heritage of the state.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board remains committed to enhancing the welfare of workers and their families through such initiatives.
